question: Which soil is acidic in nature and found in high rainfall areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Laterite soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Laterite soil** is acidic in nature and is typically found in regions with **high rainfall and high temperature**.
 
• This soil is rich in **iron and aluminum oxides**, giving it a reddish or yellowish color.
 
• **Laterite soils are poor in nutrients** like nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus, making them less fertile for agriculture without proper treatment.
 
• They are commonly found in **tropical and subtropical regions**, including parts of India such as Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha, and the hilly areas of Assam.
 
• Laterite soil is extensively used for **construction purposes** due to its hard and compact structure when dried.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acidity in Soils**:

 
 
• Acidity in soils is caused by the leaching of basic nutrients like calcium and magnesium due to heavy rainfall.
 
• Such soils tend to have a lower pH value, which impacts crop growth unless treated with lime or organic matter.
 
 
 
• **Soil Classification in India**:
 
 
• The major soil types in India include alluvial soil, black soil, red soil, laterite soil, arid soil, and forest soil.
 
• Each type of soil is associated with specific climatic and geographical conditions.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil and Agriculture**:
 
 
• Laterite soils are suitable for crops like tea, coffee, cashew, and coconut, which thrive in acidic conditions.
 
• They require significant soil management practices, such as the addition of organic compost, to improve fertility.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution in India**:
 
 
• In India, laterite soil is predominantly found in the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and parts of the northeastern states.
 
• It is also common in the southern and central regions of India, especially in areas with monsoon rainfall.
